reason: Moses is portrayed as an established national leader in this passage. He issues military commands to Joshua ('Choose men for us and go out to fight with Amalek'), Joshua follows his orders explicitly ('Joshua did as Moses told him'), and Moses positions himself as the spiritual leader of the nation by standing on the hill with God's staff. The narrative emphasizes Moses's central role in determining the battle's outcome—when he raises his hand, Israel prevails; when he lowers it, Amalek prevails. This demonstrates clear national leadership authority over military strategy and the outcome of the conflict. Moses is not aspiring to leadership but exercising it with the obedience of his subordinates.
